request.spec:
A paste box takes lines of name,amount,date,note (the note may hold commas; the date may be
blank for the sheet's today; the note may be absent) and adds a DRAFT claim per line, in order,
for the named person (the name must be on the sheet, matched as names are compared). Every line is
checked first with exactly the claim form's rules: if any line fails, an error shows on the box
and nothing is added; otherwise every claim is added and written as CLAIM_ADDED. Show how many
were added.
request.prompt:

A paste box takes lines of name,amount,date,note (the note may hold commas; the date may be

agent.result_text:
The paste box is in and all 4 acceptance tests pass on the first `bin/e2e` run.

You paste lines of `name,amount,date,note` and press the button. The server checks every line before adding anything. If all lines pass, it adds one DRAFT claim per line in the order given, and each is written to the audit file as `CLAIM_ADDED`. The box then shows how many were added and clears. If any line fails, an error shows on the box and nothing is stored or audited.

How lines are read:
- **Name:** must already be on the sheet. Spaces around it are ignored and case doesn't matter, the same way the app already compares names.
- **Fields:** a line is split at its first three commas, so any further commas stay in the note. A blank date takes the sheet's today, and the note can be left off.
- **Checks:** the amount has to fit the claim form's limits (at most two decimals). The note can be up to 500 characters. Dates in a closed period, dates after a person's retirement and negative amounts are refused, just as on the claim form.

Things I chose that the request didn't spell out:
- **Blank lines are skipped**, and a paste with no real lines is refused.
- **Negative amounts are always refused.** On the claim form a negative amount has to name the settled claim it corrects, and a pasted line has no field for that.
- **The error usually reads "Could not add the pasted claims; none were added."** The server sends back a reason that names the failing line, but by default Spring Boot leaves that text out of error responses, so it only reaches the screen if that setting is changed.

The server code is a new `paste` package (`PasteController.java`, `PasteService.java`) under `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`, with the endpoint at `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/paste`. The box itself sits under the quick-add bar in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`.
